chapters.name: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
keyPoints: y = sin⁻¹x: Domain [-1, 1], Range [-π/2, π/2], sin⁻¹(-x) = -sin⁻¹x
y = cos⁻¹x: Domain [-1, 1], Range [0, π], cos⁻¹(-x) = π - cos⁻¹x
y = tan⁻¹x: Domain ℝ, Range (-π/2, π/2), tan⁻¹(-x) = -tan⁻¹x
y = cot⁻¹x: Domain ℝ, Range (0, π), cot⁻¹(-x) = π - cot⁻¹x
y = sec⁻¹x: Domain ℝ - (-1, 1), Range [0, π] - {π/2}, sec⁻¹(-x) = π - sec⁻¹x
y = csc⁻¹x: Domain ℝ - (-1, 1), Range [-π/2, π/2] - {0}, csc⁻¹(-x) = -csc⁻¹x

chapters.name: Matrices & Determinants
keyPoints: Square matrix A symmetric ⇔ A' = A; skew-symmetric ⇔ A' = -A.
Area of triangle: Δ = ½ |x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|.
System of Linear Equations (AX = B): |A| ≠ 0 ⇒ Unique consistent solution: X = A⁻¹B.
|A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O ⇒ Inconsistent (no solution).
|A| = 0 and (adj A)B = O ⇒ Infinitely many solutions or inconsistent.

chapters.name: Calculus: Differential Calculus
keyPoints: Differentiability ⇒ Continuity (converse not true).
d/dx(sin⁻¹x) = 1/√(1 - x²), d/dx(cos⁻¹x) = -1/√(1 - x²), d/dx(tan⁻¹x) = 1/(1 + x²)
Strictly Increasing on (a, b) ⇔ f'(x) > 0; Strictly Decreasing on (a, b) ⇔ f'(x) < 0.
Critical point ⇔ f'(c) = 0 or f'(c) undefined.
1st Derivative Test: f'(x) changes + → - at c ⇒ Local Maxima; - → + at c ⇒ Local Minima.
2nd Derivative Test: f'(c) = 0, f''(c) < 0 ⇒ Local Maxima; f'(c) = 0, f''(c) > 0 ⇒ Local Minima.
Rolle's Theorem: f(a)=f(b) ⇒ f'(c) = 0 for some c ∈ (a, b).
LMVT: f'(c) = [f(b) - f(a)] / (b - a) for some c ∈ (a, b).

formulas.name: Integration by Parts
formulas.latex: \int u v \, dx = u \int v \, dx - \int \left(u' \int v \, dx\right) dx
formulas.description: ILATE preference: Inverse, Log, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential.

formulas.name: Special Form Integral
formulas.latex: \int e^x [f(x) + f'(x)] \, dx = e^x f(x) + C

formulas.name: Definite Integral Property (P3)
formulas.latex: \int_a^b f(x) \, dx = \int_a^b f(a + b - x) \, dx

formulas.name: Linear Differential Equation
formulas.latex: \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x) \implies I.F. = e^{\int P \, dx} \implies y \cdot (I.F.) = \int [Q \cdot (I.F.)] \, dx + C

keyPoints: P6: ∫(0 to 2a) f(x)dx = 2∫(0 to a) f(x)dx [if f(2a - x) = f(x)]; 0 [if f(2a - x) = -f(x)]
Area under curve: A = ∫|f(x)|dx; Area between curves: A = ∫|f(x) - g(x)|dx.
Variable Separable: ∫ h(y) dy = ∫ g(x) dx + C
Homogeneous (dy/dx = g(y/x)): Put y = vx ⇒ dy/dx = v + x (dv/dx)
Order = highest derivative; Degree = highest exponent of highest derivative in polynomial form.

formulas.name: Independent Events
formulas.latex: P(A \cap B) = P(A) P(B) \implies P(A \cup B) = 1 - P(A') P(B')

keyPoints: a ⊥ b ⇔ a · b = 0. a ∥ b ⇔ a × b = 0.
Lines intersect ⇔ (b1 × b2) · (a2 - a1) = 0.
Linear Programming: Z = ax + by subject to linear constraints.
Corner Point Theorem: Optimal value of Z always occurs at extreme vertices (corner points) of the convex feasible region.
If two vertices give same optimal Z, all points on line segment connecting them give same value.
Law of Total Probability: P(A) = Σ P(Ej) P(A|Ej).
